prompt: Company profile: Metal stamping plant in Kenosha, Wisconsin; 150 employees. Situation: A new high-tonnage press line was commissioned. Area noise monitoring in the press bay shows employee full-shift exposures around 88 dBA TWA; the rest of the plant is below 80 dBA. About 25 employees work in the press bay. Ask: Identify the compliance obligations this situation creates or affects for the compliance-obligations register. For each obligation: state the requirement, its source, its applicability to this company, the ISO clause it maps to (ISO 14001 6.1.3 / ISO 45001 6.1.3), and how and when compliance should be evaluated (9.1.2).
response:
Based on the provided scenario, here are the key compliance obligations for the metal stamping plant's register, structured as requested.

**Primary Obligation: Occupational Noise Exposure**

| Requirement | Source | Applicability | ISO Clause Mapping (14001/45001 6.1.3) | Evaluation Method & Timing (9.1.2) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Implement feasible engineering or administrative controls to reduce employee noise exposure below the Action Level (85 dBA TWA) and as low as feasible below the PEL (90 dBA TWA).** | OSHA 29 CFR 1910.95(a), (b)(1) - Occupational Noise Exposure Standard. Wisconsin may have an identical state plan. | Directly applicable. Monitoring shows exposures (~88 dBA) above the OSHA Action Level (85 dBA) for ~25 press bay employees. | **ISO 45001 6.1.3** (OH&S risks and opportunities). Noise is a significant health hazard (hearing loss). | **How:** Review noise monitoring data, engineering control implementation records, and administrative control logs. **When:** Continually during operation; formally at least annually and whenever changes occur (e.g., new equipment, process modifications). |
| **Establish and implement a Hearing Conservation Program (HCP) for all employees with exposures at or above 85 dBA TWA (8-hour).** | OSHA 29 CFR 1910.95(c) - Hearing Conservation Amendment. | Mandatory. Since exposures are above 85 dBA, a full HCP is required for affected employees. | **ISO 45001 6.1.3** (OH&S risks). Also maps to **clause 8.1.2** (eliminating hazards/ reducing OH&S risks). | **How:** Audit HCP elements: audiometric testing records, training documentation, hearing protector provision and use, and program effectiveness. **When:** Annual audit of the entire HCP; quarterly review of key metrics (e.g., audiometric results, compliance rates). |
| **Provide annual audiometric testing for all employees in the HCP.** | OSHA 29 CFR 1910.95(g) | Directly applicable to the ~25 press bay employees. | **ISO 45001 6.1.3** & **8.1.2** (controlling health risks). | **How:** Verify schedules, employee participation, and review of test results by an audiologist or physician. **When:** Annually for each enrolled employee; program effectiveness reviewed annually. |
| **Provide adequate hearing protection (with sufficient Noise Reduction Rating) and ensure its use by employees.** | OSHA 29 CFR 1910.95(i), (j) | Applicable. Required for employees exposed at or above 90 dBA, and for those between 85-90 dBA who either have not had a standard threshold shift or choose to use them. | **ISO 45001 8.1.2** (hierarchy of controls) & **7.1.4** (resources). | **How:** Observe use in the press bay, review training records, inspect PPE procurement and availability. **When:** Daily supervisory checks; formal documented inspections quarterly. |
| **Train employees on noise hazards and HCP elements annually.** | OSHA 29 CFR 1910.95(k) | Applicable to all employees in the HCP (~25). | **ISO 45001 7.3** (awareness) & **7.4** (communication). | **How:** Review training materials, attendance records, and employee comprehension. **When:** Upon initial assignment and at least annually thereafter. |

**Secondary & Related Obligations**

| Requirement | Source | Applicability | ISO Clause Mapping (14001/45001 6.1.3) | Evaluation Method & Timing (9.1.2) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Maintain accurate records of noise exposure monitoring and audiometric tests.** | OSHA 29 CFR 1910.95(m) | Directly applicable. The company has monitoring data and will generate audiometric records. | **ISO 45001 7.5** (documented information). Also **ISO 14001 6.1.3** if noise emissions to community are a concern. | **How:** Audit recordkeeping systems for completeness, accuracy, and retention (duration of employment + 30 years for audiograms). **When:** During annual management system audits. |
| **Assess and control hazards associated with the new press line installation (beyond noise).** | OSHA 29 CFR 1910.212 - General Machine Guarding, and other relevant standards. | Applicable. Commissioning new equipment triggers a requirement to ensure all associated hazards (crushing, shearing, etc.) are controlled. | **ISO 45001 6.1.2.1** (hazard identification) & **8.1.2** (hierarchy of controls). | **How:** Conduct a comprehensive machine-specific risk assessment. Inspect guarding, interlocks, and lockout/tagout procedures. **When:** Prior to operation (now) and periodically thereafter (e.g., quarterly). |
| **Evaluate environmental noise emissions to the community (if significant).** | Local Kenosha or Wisconsin DNR Noise Ordinances / Regulations. | Potentially applicable. A new high-tonnage press line may increase plant boundary noise levels, triggering permit or nuisance conditions. | **ISO 14001 6.1.3** (environmental aspects and compliance obligations). | **How:** Conduct boundary noise monitoring. Compare results to local ordinance limits. **When:** Initially after commissioning, and periodically (e.g., annually) or if complaints arise. |

**Summary for the Compliance Obligations Register:**
The commissioning of the new press line has **created a new and significant compliance obligation** regarding occupational noise, moving the company from a potential baseline condition into full **Hearing Conservation Program** requirements. It has also **affected existing obligations** related to machine safety, requiring a fresh risk assessment. The primary focus for the register must be **OSHA 29 CFR 1910.95**, with secondary attention to machine guarding and potential environmental noise regulations. Compliance evaluation will be frequent (daily, quarterly) for operational controls and at least annually for programmatic elements.
